title: Six pack keys render raw on provider-less hosts — their consumers' defaults tables lack the entry and the call sites carry no inline defaultValue (#3865 census residue)
body:
Filed by the PM seat from PR #4372's accepted census (the #3865 option-A implementation), where these six were measured and explicitly left for a follow-up: of the 26 keys read outside their hook's defaults table, 20 carried an inline `defaultValue` and were fixed by #4372's fallback order; these six carry **neither** a table entry nor an inline default, so on a provider-less host `createSafeTranslation`'s `fallbackT` returns the raw key string.

## The six (from the census — re-verify each at claim time, call sites move)

| key | consumer hook (per the census) |
|---|---|
| `detail.saving` | plugin-detail `useDetailTranslation` |
| `list.resetSortToDefault` | plugin-list `useListViewTranslation` |
| `appDesigner.widgetProperties` | plugin-designer `useDesignerTranslation` |
| `appDesigner.addWidget` | plugin-designer `useDesignerTranslation` |
| `appDesigner.modeEdit` | plugin-designer `useDesignerTranslation` |
| `common.delete` | (census: outside-table without default — locate the actual call site) |

## Fix shape

Add each key to its consumer's module-local defaults table, **byte-identical to the en pack value** per each map's docblock contract (mechanically enforced for some maps — see objectui#3440's precedent). No pack edits, no new keys, no call-site changes. Red-first per key: a provider-less render asserting the raw key pre-fix, the en value post-fix (the #4372 test file has the mounting pattern).

Alternative for any key whose census attribution turns out stale (consumer gone, key retired): record the measurement instead of forcing an entry.

## Why now

PR #4372 made inline defaults live, but these six have no fallback of any kind — they are the census's only remaining raw-key renders. Small, mechanical, fully enumerated.

Related: #3865 / PR #4372 (census source), #3810 (closed — its option C must not be revived as written), #3440 (byte-identity enforcement precedent).
